text:
Cutter Gauthier has scored in nine straight games, 16 goals in all, and has a point in eleven straight. That is the story the Ducks bring to St. Louis, and the part we like best is that it holds up: over his last ten games he has 6.2 expected goals on his own shots, against 4.7 at his usual rate, and his ice time is up a minute and a half a night. Expected goals measure the quality of the chances, so this is a player getting to better spots more often, not just a hot stick. Beckett Sennecke has 17 points in his last ten alongside him, though our numbers flag him as due to cool.

The streak runs into the goalie who has been the Blues' best player lately. Joel Hofer is .922 on the season and 8.4 goals saved above expected, and .932 over his last five starts, including a 29-save shutout of Utah that ended in an eight-round shootout. That he holds the net at all says something about the other storyline in St. Louis: Jordan Binnington has spent the last two weeks in trade-rumor headlines, from the Oilers to the Rangers, while Hofer has taken the starts.

There is a homecoming too. Mason McTavish, drafted third overall by Anaheim in 2021, faces the Ducks for the first time since leaving them after 304 games in their colors. Ross Johnston, 173 games a Duck, makes the same trip.

The matchup in net tilts hard toward St. Louis. Lukas Dostal is .856 and 5.1 goals worse than expected this season, .832 over his last five. Anaheim also takes 4.8 penalties a game, the kind of habit that keeps a team chasing. Our numbers have it close anyway: 3.24 expected goals for the Blues, 3.05 for the Ducks. Anaheim plays without Ryan Poehling (knee, on injured reserve), with Leo Carlsson moved into his spot beside Nesterenko and Killorn; St. Louis is without Dillon Dube.
headline: Gauthier's streak walks into Joel Hofer's crease
